newsitem.title: UK: Costain revamps as losses rise.
newsitem.headline: Costain revamps as losses rise.

text.p: British engineering and construction company Costain Group announced on Tuesday two asset sales and top board changes, after becoming aware of "significantly" greater losses than forecast.

Costain said it was selling its U.S. coal units to Rencoal Inc of the U.S. for 28.6 million stg an its one-third stake in the Spitalfields development site to Malaysia's Metacorp for 23.4 million stg.
"Since the announcement of its interim results, the group has become aware of losses significantly greater than forecast," the company said in a statement.
U.S. Coal, which the company said had encountered worse than anticipated geological conditions resulting in production difficulties, which would impact its trading result by 11 million stg.
The company said it had suffered more losses than expected in three contracts in its Middle East construction business, which would lead to losses of four million stg more than earlier feared.

Sale proceeds from U.S. Coal would be used to reduce its U.S. debt and help it to fund some continuing obligations linked to U.S. Coal, put at 12.2-15.2 million stg. These obligations should be cleared by end 1997.
Proceeds from the sale of Spitalfields would be used to reduce group debt and help fund future working capital needs.

Costain added it has conditional option agreements with Indonesian industrialist Hendri Luhur and Mohamed Abdulmohsin Kharafi & Sons WLL, for them to subscribe to 13.4 million new shares to meet its additional financial requirements. The shares would be offered at 40-50p each, for a total 5.4 million stg cash, between March 1 and June 30, 1997.
The subscription by Kuwait's Kharafi & Sons would enable them to maintain their shareholding at 25.35 percent.
Trading in the company's share price was suspended on November 7, 1996 when it was quoted at 46 pence.

Costain said the net assets of the group were less than 50 percent of its called up share capital. An extraordinary general meeting has been convened to consider this position and seek shareholder approval for the proposed sales of U.S. Coal and Spitalfields.

The company's said it intends to seek a lifting of its London share supension, in effect since November 7, once its financial position has been clarified. But, this is unlikely to be before completion of the U,S, Coal sale, which is targeted for the end of December.
The company said its chairman Christopher Benson would step down and would be replaced by Azman Firdaus bin Shafii, the current deputy chairman, with effect from January 1, 1997.
Alan Lovell, the chief executive has decided to step down from his post of chief executive but would stay with the group until his successor was found.
